title: Foundations of Cell and Molecular Biology
description: From molecular structure to cell behavior: build a mechanistic model of how living systems store information, capture energy, and maintain boundaries.

modifications: Normalized the course title to Foundations of Cell and Molecular Biology; the stable ID is unchanged.

outcomes.description: Use free-energy and enzyme models to reason about cellular reactions.
Trace information flow from DNA to phenotype.
Interpret controls and evidence in a simple molecular experiment.

lesson_objectives.description: Distinguish covalent structure from molecular interactions.
Predict how charge, polarity, and hydrophobicity shape biomolecular assembly.
Use covalent structure and functional groups to identify chemical features that may change under a specified mutation.
Use pH relative to pKa to predict the dominant protonation state of a simple ionizable group.
Use residue environment and measurement context to make a bounded prediction about a protein substitution.
Use matched abundance, folding, and activity measurements to separate candidate mechanisms of a protein variant.
Use electrochemical gradients to determine passive ion movement.
Separate simple diffusion, facilitated diffusion, and active transport.
Interpret Michaelis-Menten parameters without confusing affinity and rate.
Relate ΔG to equilibrium and coupling.
Trace DNA information through transcription and translation.
Identify the purpose of positive, negative, and loading controls.
Summarize replicate-level data without turning a descriptive contrast into a causal conclusion.

duration.equivalent_structure: Proposed undergraduate 14-week scope only. Weeks 1 and 2 have four developed lessons. Compact legacy readings remain in weeks 4 and 7; weeks 3, 5 through 6, and 8 through 14 are outlines without authored lesson sequences or summative assessments. Workload is not measured, so this plan is not evidence of semester equivalence.

weeks.title: Covalent architecture, functional groups, water, and molecular interactions
Protein sequence and structure; membranes and transport
Enzyme kinetics, free energy, and cellular energetics
Cell imaging, fractionation, and measurement limits
DNA structure, replication, repair, and genome organization
RNA processing, translation, and protein turnover
Cell-cycle control, senescence, and cell death
Development, cell fate, and stem-cell concepts
Integrated experimental design and evidence synthesis

workload.basis: Not measured. Legacy nominal credit and display-time labels are not retained as workload estimates.

lessons.title: Covalent architecture, functional groups, and biological molecules
lessons.worked_example: For a cysteine-to-serine substitution, compare thiol and hydroxyl chemistry and ask whether a disulfide is plausible in the relevant compartment. If activity falls, compare soluble and insoluble fractions and include a matched wild-type control before attributing the effect to loss of disulfide formation.

lessons.title: Water, pH, and noncovalent interactions
lessons.worked_example: At pH 7.4 with pKa 6.0, the two-state acid model gives [A-]/[HA] about 25 and a protonated fraction about 0.038. Calculate the population from the ratio, then state why this solution estimate may not transfer unchanged to a folded protein whose local environment shifts pKa.

modules.title: Protein sequence, structure, and variant evidence

lessons.title: Protein sequence, structure, and variant evidence
lessons.worked_example: With a buried leucine-to-aspartate variant, destabilization is plausible, not inevitable. Compare soluble abundance, folding, and specific activity at matched protein concentration to distinguish altered stability from catalytic effects and avoid inferring a phenotype from sequence alone.

lessons.title: Membranes, transport, and electrochemical gradients
lessons.worked_example: For 5 mM K+ outside and 140 mM inside at 25 C, the ideal monovalent-ion Nernst potential is about -89 mV. At that voltage, the single-ion electrochemical terms balance even though concentrations differ; this value does not predict the whole-cell voltage or flux rate.

lessons.title: Enzymes and cellular energetics
lessons.worked_example: If [S] = Km, the model predicts v = Vmax/2. Doubling enzyme concentration doubles Vmax but leaves Km unchanged in the simple model.

lessons.title: Gene expression and experimental logic
lessons.worked_example: In a knockdown experiment, a non-targeting RNA control tests for delivery or off-target effects; a rescue with a perturbation-resistant construct strengthens causal attribution.

grading_policy.attempt_policy: Unlimited formative retries; no summative grade is awarded.
grading_policy.solution_release: Public practice solutions may be shown after an attempt. They are not production exam keys.
grading_policy.late_policy: No deadlines or late penalties exist in this partial package.
grading_policy.appeals: Learners may request one human review per attempt; operator-provisioned reviewers can decide only when the installed question specification matches the saved attempt. This workflow does not provide course-level human grading.

accessibility.diagram_policy: The seed package contains no imported diagrams; newly authored diagrams require descriptions and individual license tracking.
known_issues: Unicode equations require structured mathematical alternatives and assistive-technology review.

history.summary: Drafted a 14-week scope and outcome-to-assessment crosswalk, developed two substantial lessons in each of weeks 1 and 2, and added original formative questions and retrieval cards; the course remains partial.
Added an original, size-limited CSV summary-table exercise with deterministic numeric-cell checks; the package remains partial.
Added an original four-criterion structured experimental-reasoning practice item with deterministic rubric scoring; the course remains partial.
Added three authored, reproducibly selected forms of the first formative item; attempts pin the selected variant specification.
Added one original multiple-select practice item with transparent partial credit and explicit learner enrollment updates between content versions.
Preserved original compact prototype content in separate manifests and readings; labeled partial without semester or credit equivalency.
Normalized the course title to Foundations of Cell and Molecular Biology; the stable ID is unchanged.

limitations: The proposed 14-week scope is not 14 weeks of instruction: only weeks 1 and 2 have two substantial lessons, while compact enzyme and gene-expression prototypes remain in weeks 4 and 7.
There is no authored substantive homework sequence, three-activity laboratory sequence, midterm, cumulative final, or integrative project.
Current formative checks across six lessons do not demonstrate comprehensive outcome coverage or mastery; some lesson objectives remain unassessed.
Bloom labels and structured prerequisite edges are initial authoring classifications awaiting subject-matter review.
Question answers and solution feedback are intentionally public practice authoring specifications, not restricted exam keys.
Numerical specifications preserve the prototype's tolerance and optional unit entry; significant-figure and dimensional checks have not been authored.
Total workload and weekly study hours are unknown; former nominal credit values and hardcoded reading times do not establish workload.
The CSV practice item checks four numeric summary cells only; it does not grade scripts, arbitrary data analysis, uncertainty analysis, or causal reasoning.
intentionally_omitted: Lessons and assessments for most proposed weeks, summative course assessments, and the complete semester workflow are intentionally not represented as finished content.
